title: Move the chattic.us hosted zone to the management account
description:
Ryan decided (2026-09-30, closed 8db911): the chattic.us zone lives in the new management account. Route 53 cannot move a zone between accounts; the process is to create a new zone there, copy the records, verify, then change the name servers at the registrar (outside Route 53, Ryan only).

## Steps
1. Create the hosted zone in the management account (profile management). Note the four new name servers.
2. Copy the 20 record sets verbatim (aliases to CloudFront, the two ACM validation CNAMEs; the NS and SOA at the apex are created by Route 53 itself and must NOT be copied). No MX or TXT exist.
3. Verify with dig against each new name server that every name returns the same answer as the live zone.
4. Ryan changes the NS records at the registrar to the new four. The apex NS TTL is 172800 (48h), so both zones must serve identical records until old resolvers age out; keep the legacy zone until then.
5. Only after a quiet period remove the legacy zone. It is owned by the ChatticusDns stack, so that stack must not be deleted or destroyed while it still matters; do not delete the zone by hand.

## Consequences and traps (from the read-only survey)
- Legacy CloudFormation stacks own record sets in the OLD zone: ChatticusMarketing (4), each ChatticusWeb* and ChatticusAuth* (2 each). After the name-server switch the old zone is no longer authoritative, so a legacy deploy that replaces a CloudFront distribution and its alias record would silently not take effect and could cause an outage. Freeze any legacy change that replaces a distribution during the switch window, or do the switch when the environments have moved.
- The marketing site is a separate private repo (Chattic.us-web, stack ChatticusMarketing, apex and www and its ACM validation records). This repo cannot change it. That repo needs its own plan for records in a zone in another account; raise it with Ryan before the switch. Its ACM certificates renew through the validation CNAMEs, so those two records MUST exist in the new zone.
- Environment accounts each need a certificate for their own names (CloudFront requires us-east-1) and alias records. Options: (a) delegate each environment's names to a small zone in that account by NS records in the management zone (dev., auth-dev. for development, etc.; no cross-account writes at deploy time; recommended), or (b) keep every record in the management zone and have the environment accounts write them through a cross-account role. Needs Ryan's choice before the first environment deploy.
- Google OAuth redirect URIs and the Cognito custom auth domains are tied to the auth hostnames and must be re-registered per environment when those move.

## Done when
The management-account zone answers every name identically, the registrar points at it, dig from outside confirms it, the marketing site and dev/staging/hey/auth hostnames still resolve, and the legacy zone is left in place until the quiet period ends.

comments.author: home
comments.text: DECIDED by Ryan (2026-09-30): the main chattic.us zone lives in the management account AND each environment's names are DELEGATED to small zones in that environment's own account (option (a) on this card): development gets dev. and auth-dev. zones in chatticus-development, staging gets staging. and auth-staging., production gets hey. and auth.. The management zone holds the apex, www (marketing), and NS delegation records for those six names; the environment accounts issue their own CloudFront certificates validated inside their own delegated zones, so no cross-account record writing is needed at deploy time. Consequence for the first environment deploy (fd3724): the ChatticusDns stack must become per-account (it currently creates the apex zone and a certificate for the apex), and the delegation NS records are a one-time step in the management zone per name, done once the environment account's zone exists and before its distribution is pointed at. Sequencing stays: zone move first (this card), then delegations as each environment is brought up.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Started 2026-09-30 (Ryan: start the zone move; reminded that this project is IaC only). Approach: the zone and its records are a reviewed CDK stack, never hand-made. (1) DONE: cdk bootstrap in the management account (CDKToolkit CREATE_COMPLETE v32), the one AWS write so far. (2) IN PROGRESS: new stack ChatticusManagementDns (PublicHostedZone chattic.us, RemovalPolicy RETAIN, termination protection) holding the 18 records exported read-only from the legacy zone: 8 names x A/AAAA aliases to CloudFront (hosted zone Z2FDTNDATAQYW2, no health evaluation) and the two ACM validation CNAMEs. Record data is generated from the live export and asserted uniform. Tests assert every record and that apex NS/SOA are NOT declared (Route 53 owns them). Instantiated only with -c managementDns=true so it never appears in a legacy synth. The 8 web/auth/marketing alias records are TRANSITIONAL: each environment's names are replaced by NS delegations as that environment moves (per the delegation decision). (3) After merge: deploy once from Ryan's non-root SSO session with a guard, then verify every name with dig against the four new name servers BEFORE anything points at them. The registrar NS change stays Ryan's.

comments.author: home
comments.text: STEPS 1-3 DONE 2026-09-30. #376 merged (145753b); ChatticusManagementDns deployed once from Ryan's non-root management SSO session (guard: account is the Organization's management account, not legacy), records read from a local export kept outside the repo. The zone exists in the management account but NOTHING delegates to it yet, so no live traffic is affected. VERIFIED before any switch: (1) exact read-back of the new zone from Route 53 vs the legacy export: 18 records each, only-in-legacy none, only-in-new none, content differences none (apex NS/SOA created by Route 53). (2) dig against every record at each of the four new name servers: 72 queries, 0 failures, all authoritative NOERROR with answers; both ACM validation CNAMEs identical across the four servers and equal to the legacy zone's answers. (3) DNSSEC is NOT in use (legacy zone NOT_SIGNING, no DS at the parent), so a name-server change cannot break validation. Hosted zone id Z01889361LM45L22GZQ4Y. NEW NAME SERVERS for the registrar: ns-695.awsdns-22.net, ns-335.awsdns-41.com, ns-1876.awsdns-42.co.uk, ns-1399.awsdns-46.org. Current (legacy) delegation, to keep for rollback: ns-1030.awsdns-00.org, ns-2025.awsdns-61.co.uk, ns-204.awsdns-25.com, ns-836.awsdns-40.net. REMAINING: (4) Ryan changes the four name servers at the registrar (outside Route 53; the domain is not registered in Route 53 in either account); delegation is cached up to 48h, both zones serve identical records meanwhile so there is no outage window; (5) after a quiet period, confirm with dig from outside that the new servers are authoritative, then leave the legacy zone in place (it is owned by the ChatticusDns stack, do not delete by hand) until the legacy environments are retired. ROLLBACK: put the four legacy name servers back at the registrar. Until step 5 completes, do not deploy legacy changes that REPLACE a CloudFront distribution (the alias would change only in the old zone).

comments.author: home
comments.text: STEP 4 DONE 2026-09-30. Ryan changed the four name servers at the registrar. The .us registry showed the change about 11 minutes later (the earlier check still showed the old set, which is normal registrar latency). Verified from outside afterwards: registry delegation = the four new name servers; all eight names (apex, www, dev, staging, hey, auth-dev, auth-staging, auth) resolve A and AAAA through 8.8.8.8 and return HTTP 200; SOA primary shows the NEW zone at 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1 while 9.9.9.9 still serves its cached OLD delegation (expected; both zones hold identical records, verified, so there is no outage window). REMAINING (step 5): after the old delegation has aged out (up to about 48 hours, so on or after 2026-10-02) confirm all three public resolvers answer from the new zone, then leave the legacy zone in place: it is owned by the ChatticusDns stack in the legacy account and is removed with that stack when the legacy environments are retired, never by hand. Until then do not deploy a legacy change that REPLACES a CloudFront distribution (192cad tracks the marketing stack's records). Rollback if ever needed: restore the four legacy name servers at the registrar.
